x-bump-note: 8.1.0 -> 8.2.0 (nested-field-additive) adds four fields, upstream-first, in reply to cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-19-claude-klabauter-em-baton-schema-bump-role-axis-and-pickup-doctrine.md (asks 1 and 2). `plan_ids` / `deliverable_ids` are nullable-or-array plural siblings of `origin_plan_id` / `deliverable_id` respectively, same string shape on every entry as the singular field each mirrors; both singulars are retained unchanged, nothing is removed, no `required` entry, no cross-field `allOf` coupling. `baton_role` (enum: work | record, optional, absence ≡ unknown and unknown is NOT inheritable) is the inheritability axis ratified by state/subagent-share/bc70d292-1669-4531-aaa9-845c1b8bb79c/coordinatoreng-director-d8ff2cfd.md: distinct from `kind` (provenance) and from `handoff_phase` (the plan→execute seam, whose `execution` value is deliberately NOT reused here to avoid a same-block naming collision) — see this field's own description for the full ruling. No backfill: `handoff.normalize` must never stamp `baton_role` onto an existing record: this bump is optional-additive text everywhere in one JSON Schema, so nothing here enforces that discipline at the schema layer, but it is stated as read-side contract in the field's own description and any writer touching this field is bound by it. PRIOR: 8.0.0 -> 8.1.0 (nested-field-additive) adopts `reconcile_disposition` / `reconcile_disposition_reason` upstream from claude-klabauter's vendored copy, which already carried both (read by `coordinator_core/ops/handoff_reconcile.py`'s `_check_conservation` D1 assertion). Both are optional top-level strings, no `required` entry, no cross-field `allOf` coupling — text matched to claude-klabauter's committed-HEAD byte-for-byte on the shape, descriptions unchanged. Resolves ask 4 of cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-14-claude-klabauter-em-reviewed-range-pattern-and-direction-blind-parity-gate.md: the EM's ruling is that handoff frontmatter shape is DoE-authored doctrine-plane surface, so a field claude-klabauter's engine reads belongs upstream rather than as a declared fork-with-tolerance. Closes the vendored-shape parity gap that memo's item 3 reported (claude-klabauter was AHEAD, not behind, on these two fields — the parity gate's own direction-blindness is a separate open ask on claude-klabauter's gate implementation, not addressed by this bump). Companion bump: handoff-archived.schema.json 2.5.0 -> 2.6.0 declares the same pair for the archived sibling. PRIOR: 7.1.0 -> 8.0.0 (producer-axis-collapse-narrow) removes `hand-authored` from the `x-producer-typed-command.mapping` vocabulary, taking it from 49 members to 48, and rewrites the two descriptions that named it. The removal itself landed at 711ea128f under an UNMOVED 7.1.0 — this bump is that omission being corrected, not a second change. WHY THE OMISSION WAS A DEFECT, stated plainly because the temptation to re-make it is real: the member was unreachable (claude-klabauter's `producer_resolve.resolve_producer_for_creation` yields only a command string, `unresolved`, or `None` on that axis; their `producer_vocab` contract block states `hand-authored`'s truth-condition does not depend on `typed_command`; their `test_producer_axis_entity` pins the state as `{op_identity: hand-authored, typed_command: None}`), and unreachability made the change SEMANTICALLY inert — but the vendored-shape gates on both sides hash BYTES, not reachability, and deliberately so: whether a consumer could have held a value is exactly the judgment a shape gate refuses to make on a version string's behalf. 7.1.0 had already been vendored by claude-klabauter (their b50f4dd0c) when the removal landed, so the narrow moved shape under a version a consumer was already holding. That deadlocked both repos: their `test_vendored_schema_shape_bump_parity` refuses to import a shape move at an unmoved version, and this repo's `test_vendored_schema_version_parity.py:170` asserts version equality hard, so neither side could clear it alone. Raised by claude-klabauter-em in cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-13-claude-klabauter-em-handoff-schema-version-move-is-yours-and-a-retraction.md; they agree the removal is correct and asked only for the version to move. CLASSIFIED MAJOR, not minor, and the argument for minor was weighed and rejected: no consumer can break, since nothing in either tree READS this mapping (only a keyword-coverage allowlist names it there, and test_handoff_producer_vocabulary_parity here). But the bump-class vocabulary (coordinator/docs/wiki/schema-version-gate.md) is closed at four terms and defines `major` as 'a field removed, or existing semantics changed' — a declared vocabulary member being removed is exactly that, and this file's own 3.1.0 -> 4.0.0 entry already classed a vocabulary narrow major. Annotation-ness does not soften the class either: the 3.0.0 -> 3.1.0 x-baton-class entry explicitly declined to let non-record-validating status change a class, taking nested-field-additive on its own shape-of-change merits. Consumer-envelope cost of the major digit was checked rather than assumed: claude-klabauter is the only genuine vendoring consumer (claude-klabauter is their publish mirror, not a peer), and they requested the move and re-vendor on landing. BUNDLED, and the most-restrictive class governs the whole commit: `additional_predecessors.description` adopts claude-klabauter's sedge-02 amendment (cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-13-claude-klabauter-em-adopt-additional-predecessors-engine-derived-correction.md) — the removed 'requires explicit PM direction' clause described a workflow that does not exist, since baton_assemble writes the field at successor-scaffold time. That half is description-only and earns no class of its own; it is adopted upstream here specifically because a description-level fork is invisible to a direct-copy re-vendor and had already been clobbered and restored once (their 1825e7771). DR-097 push-side duty attaches (major is holding on this axis): discharged by the reply memo to claude-klabauter-em stating this CLASS, not merely that a bump occurred. Full prior-version history: coordinator/schemas/SCHEMA-BUMP-HISTORY.md section handoff.schema.json.

x-baton-class.description: DERIVED-field lookup (D2) -- baton_class is NEVER written to on-disk frontmatter; a consuming function computes it on read by indexing this map with the record's own `kind` value: `x_baton_class['mapping'][record['kind']]`. Direction chosen deliberately as kind -> class, not class -> kinds: the caller of this derivation always already holds a record with a `kind` value in hand and wants its class, which is a direct O(1) lookup in this direction; the inverse (class -> kinds) would force every caller to build its own inverted index from this same data before it could answer the question it actually has. Three classes, closed set: continuation (session-handoff, recovery), deflection (spinoff, goal-seed), intention (roadmap-baton, roadmap-seed) -- see docs/plans/2026-07-29-baton-kind-vocabulary-one-axis-per-field.md § D2 for the axis rationale. The `mapping` below names the D1 TARGET names (goal-seed, roadmap-baton, roadmap-seed) -- the C10 enum narrow that admits them into this schema's own `kinds` array and `properties.kind.enum` above (retiring spinoff-goal/spinoff-roadmap/spinoff-roadmap-creator) has landed as of the 3.1.0 -> 4.0.0 bump below. A schema-parity test (coordinator/tests/) asserts every kind named here is a member of the known-kind universe (union of `kinds`/`properties.kind.enum` and this migration's D1 target table), that every class is one of the three above, and that no kind is double-assigned. `recovery` is retained per C1a's KEEP disposition (state/plan-sidecars/2026-07-29-baton-kind-vocabulary.recovery-disposition.md) rather than struck as a dead value. If a genuinely separate artifact is ever wanted for another tool's consumption (e.g. Example-retrieval-repo), it MUST be GENERATED from this mapping with its own parity test against this key -- never hand-authored independently, which is exactly the two-sources-of-truth drift this migration exists to close.

x-producer-typed-command.description: Closed vocabulary for the `producer.typed_command` axis (D6, renamed from `typed-ceremony`) — declared ONCE here, following the `x-baton-class` precedent above, rather than written out longhand the way `kind` is. `producer.typed_command` names the coordinator command verb this session was last inside when a baton was minted; it is one of two axes on the `producer` namespaced record (the other, op-identity, is not enumerated here). Enum order is APPENDED, never re-sorted — `_schema_shape.py::_semantic_shape_hash` hashes enum list order verbatim, so a set-equal reorder reds EQUAL_VERSION_SHAPE_DRIFT. This mapping's keys, in insertion order, ARE that canonical order: the 46 coordinator command verbs (alphabetical, derived from `coordinator/commands/*.md` at authoring time, D4's RESOLVED (A)), followed by the two structural members `other-command`, `unresolved` in that fixed order. `hand-authored` is NOT a member of this axis — op-identity (no ceremony ran; a human authored the record directly) is `producer.op_identity`'s value, not `producer.typed_command`'s; the two axes were split precisely so that fact lives on exactly one of them (D6/F3). Each entry carries a `group` hint so a consuming facet control can group/default-suppress without hand-maintaining a parallel 46-row table that drifts behind the command set — one of ten groups: `session`, `baton`, `planning`, `review`, `execution`, `maintenance`, `research`, `release`, `setup` for the 46 verbs (grouped by ceremony purpose), and `structural` for the two non-verb members. `other-command` means a typed slash command outside coordinator's own set (harness/other-plugin verbs like /clear, /code-review, /loop) — NOT a catch-all for an unnamed coordinator ceremony, which would be a bug. Read-side contract: `unresolved` is a defect marker — the field was expected to resolve and did not — and MUST NEVER be treated as a user-facing facet member alongside the real command verbs; a fail-closed consumer that has never seen the value would otherwise render it as a legitimate bucket. Spec backlink: pln-producer-axis-on-the-baton-con-b68971 § D4, D6.

description: Active handoff baton — carries session-continuation state for /pickup and workstream tracking. Cross-field rules (deployment_state gates, graph-primitive kind-gate, category/summary cutoff, spinoff-with-predecessor, supersedes kind-gate, handoff_phase stamp-required-when-execution, handoff_phase kind-gate) live in CROSS_FIELD_RULES['handoff'] in bin/lib/schema.js and are applied automatically by validateRecord. Origin-axis rules (kind-prefixed id well-formedness, per-kind cardinality, direct self-reference rejection, predecessor:none invariant for spinoff kinds, forked_from/origin_handoff never-silently-disagree invariant) are also in CROSS_FIELD_RULES['handoff'] (C2). Backfill policy: pre-existing forks carry null for all origin_* fields; no migration. Record-level provenance (ProvenanceEnvelope — how the pipeline observed/derived this record) is DISTINCT from artifact-level origin_* (what spawned this fork) — same word, different plane; origin_* stays frontmatter-only and is not projected into the ProvenanceEnvelope. Spec backlink: pln-structured-originating-session-8b505c § Field shape

branch.description: Git branch this handoff was created on.

status.description: Lifecycle state (DR-084 P4 narrow). Only 'open'/'claimed' admitted.

predecessor.description: Predecessor handoff path, or null/"none" for spinoffs. Key must always be present (string-or-null, D9 nullable rule).

predecessor_id.description: ID-companion for predecessor (C2, add-not-swap) — the predecessor's handoff_id, resolved and stamped at author time from the SAME predecessor the path field names (never a different one; the adjacency-inference ban is unaffected). Path-independent, survives predecessor archival/rename — the mechanism a machine walks; predecessor remains the human-legible display string. Null when the predecessor has no handoff_id (pre-existing artifact, no backfill) or predecessor is none/null. Never-silently-disagree cross-field rule (predecessor/predecessor_id must resolve to the same artifact when both non-null) is owned by C3, not this schema file. Spec backlink: pln-lifecycle-vocab-c2-durable-cro-991bd4 § C2

consumed_by.description: Session id of the consuming /pickup invocation; sourced from $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID with .current-session-id fallback.

consumed_at.description: Timestamp when the handoff was consumed (ISO 8601 date-time). Stamped by cs_consume_handoff for race-forensics precision.

claimed_by.description: Session id of the claiming /pickup invocation (DR-084 successor of consumed_by; new-vocabulary records use this). Sourced from $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID with .current-session-id fallback. Cross-field rule (claimed + claimed_at ⇒ claimed_by required) lands at P4.

claimed_at.description: Timestamp when the handoff was claimed (ISO 8601 date-time; DR-084 successor of consumed_at). Stamped by the claim transition for race-forensics precision.

reaped_from_session.description: Session id of the DEAD holder whose claim a crash-orphan reaper released, preserved at strip time so the fact of prior consumption survives the strip. Written by claude-klabauter's `_unclaim` inside the same mutate closure that removes the claim vocabulary (claimed_by/claimed_at/consumed_by/consumed_at) — a second write would reproduce the bug it fixes on a crash between the two. Distinct from claimed_by: claimed_by names the LIVE holder, reaped_from_session names a holder already gone. Its presence is forensic provenance ONLY and asserts nothing about completion — a reaped baton re-advertises as available work, and nothing here proves that work was finished (claude-klabauter's drift sweep surfaces the population in a `reaped_orphan` bucket and deliberately never closes one). Absent on every baton that was never reaped.

machine.description: Machine identifier (host name) where the session ran.

kind.description: Handoff kind. Cross-field rules enforce kind-specific constraints (graph primitives require roadmap-baton, supersedes requires spinoff, spinoff/goal-seed/roadmap-seed requires predecessor=none/null). recovery: requires predecessor: <crashed-sha> or null (no cross-field rule enforced, convention only).

authoring_session.description: Session id that authored this handoff. Required by convention on spinoffs as audit trail back to origin. On kind: session-handoff, coordinator-doc-new's scaffolder stamps this machine-generated at scaffold time (omitted, not PLACEHOLDER, when no session id is resolvable) -- coordinator_core.baton_assemble's cross-authorship adoption predicate (_adopt_prior_attempt_scaffold_path) gates adoption of a prior attempt's scaffold on this field matching the resuming run's own session id.

workstream.description: Short slug grouping related forks. Required by convention on spinoffs.

producer.description: Namespaced RESOLVED-side producer record (D5, D6) — the seam-resolved counterpart to session-shape.schema.json's capture-side `producer` (typed_command + captured_at). Additive and optional at the top level: a pre-existing record written before this bump omits the key entirely, and the batch `handoff.normalize` sweep must never backfill it onto such a record (F1) — this key's own absence is therefore a legitimate, non-defect state, distinct from the present-as-null discipline that governs its two sub-fields once the key IS written. Written at construction time by `handoff_author_fork.py` / `queue_scaffold_baton.py` only (D5); the batch normalize handler always passes producer=None and never re-resolves it for an existing record. Carries two independent axes, both required once the object is present, neither absent-as-omitted (D9): `typed_command` — which coordinator command verb (or `other-command` / `unresolved`) this session was last inside when the baton was minted; vocabulary declared ONCE at `x-producer-typed-command` above (D6, renamed from `typed-ceremony`) — reference that declaration, do not restate its 48 members here, the way `kind`'s enum wrongly is. `op_identity` — machine-vs-human, resolved reliably at the creation seam (`queue_scaffold_baton` is machine-minted by construction; a hand-edited file entering `_normalize_one_text` is not) — the field a consumer's default-suppress logic should key on, replacing the `session-op`-nature proxy. Present-as-null, never an absent key (D9, AC-2): a machine-minted baton from a session that typed no slash command still emits `typed_command: null` with `op_identity: "machine-minted"`, distinguishable from a hand-authored record (`op_identity: "hand-authored"`, `typed_command` conventionally null) and from a resolution failure (`typed_command: "unresolved"`) — three states, never collapsed to one bare `null` (AC-3, F3). Spec backlink: pln-producer-axis-on-the-baton-con-b68971 § D5, D6, D9.

typed_command.description: One of the 48 members declared once at `x-producer-typed-command` above (46 coordinator command verbs, alphabetical, plus `other-command`, `unresolved` in that fixed order), or `null` when `op_identity` is `machine-minted` and no slash command was typed this session (D3's corrected staleness bound), or when `op_identity` is `hand-authored` (conventionally null; op-identity's own axis carries that fact, not this one) — present-as-null (D9), never an absent key. `unresolved` is a defect marker, never a legitimate facet member — see the read-side contract in `x-producer-typed-command.description`.

op_identity.description: The machine-vs-human axis (D6, F3), resolved at the creation seam independent of what the session typed: `machine-minted` for a baton minted by `queue_scaffold_baton` / `handoff_author_fork`; `hand-authored` for a hand-edited file entering `_normalize_one_text` — true regardless of `typed_command`'s value, which is what makes `hand-authored` reachable independently of a mis-collapsed `null`.

repo.description: Repo id for install-leg spinoff batons (kind: spinoff seeded by a downstream installer).

install_chain_order.description: Relative install position for install-leg spinoffs (lower = earlier; coordinator = 0).

pickup_ready.description: Positive pickup-authorized signal. Absence triggers a non-blocking warning at /pickup time.

deployment_state.description: Lifecycle readiness state. DR-084 P4 narrow: 'abandoned' is retired; 'continued' (succession terminal) and 'closed' (deliberate stop, human/session only) are its replacements. Conditional-required coupling (continued→continued_into, closed→closed_reason) also lands at this narrow. Existing cross-field rules unchanged: awaiting_gate→gate_dependency required; ready_to_fire→gate_dependency forbidden; shipped→shipped_in required (post-cutoff).

gate_dependency.description: DEPRECATED (C2) — superseded by blocked_by/no_longer_blocked_by/gate_cleared_by, which admit handoff_id values alongside stub_id and give the gate a resolvable index instead of a free-text one-liner. Old values retired in spirit, not schema-enforced-retired: existing awaiting_gate records still populate this field and it remains shape-valid, but new authoring should prefer blocked_by. NOT UNCONDITIONALLY REQUIRED (C3): an awaiting_gate record must carry AT LEAST ONE of gate_dependency, non-empty blocked_by, or non-empty blocking_notes — a record with none of the three still fails. That three-way OR is enforced in the Python cross-field layer only (H-CROSS-1), NOT in this file's allOf, which encodes just the ready_to_fire-forbids-gate_dependency twin; stated here so a schema-only reader is not misled. Path-shaped values are now REJECTED (C2b, H-CROSS-9): a value containing 'tasks/' or 'archive/', or ending '.md', fails validation — put the baton dependency in blocked_by as a slug and any advisory prose in blocking_notes. Formerly: 'Required when deployment_state=awaiting_gate. One-liner naming the subsystem or condition that gates this handoff. Must be subsystem-named, not file-pathed.'

no_longer_blocked_by.description: Predecessors verified shipped — entries MOVE here from blocked_by (never dropped): a resolution relocates one blocked_by entry into no_longer_blocked_by, it does not delete it from either array. The union of blocked_by and no_longer_blocked_by is invariant across a resolution — same total membership, entries just migrate columns as their blockers clear. Same slug shape as blocked_by (stub_id or handoff_id).

blocking_notes.description: Advisory prose, NEVER read by the resolver — inert by construction. Home for the 'needs a Windows box' class of real-but-not-a-dependency constraint: true and worth recording, but not a blocked_by/no_longer_blocked_by entry because nothing on the graph clears it. Do not encode anything here that the resolver is meant to act on — that belongs in blocked_by.

gate_cleared_by.description: SHA provenance — which commit(s) discharged the gate. Written by _gate_cascade_clear; previously drifted onto disk undeclared (no additionalProperties:false to catch it) before this schema named it. Distinct from no_longer_blocked_by: gate_cleared_by answers 'which commit discharged the gate', no_longer_blocked_by answers 'which baton used to block' (slug history, not commit provenance). Both ship — they answer different questions, neither substitutes for the other.

reconcile_disposition.description: Operator-recorded disposition clearing a D1 'severed-observer' conservation violation -- read by coordinator_core/ops/handoff_reconcile.py's `_check_conservation` (D1 assertion) via the module-level `_DISPOSITION_FIELD` constant. D1 flags any handoff that surfaced in a prior reconcile pass and is still open with no recorded disposition; `_has_recorded_disposition` treats this field and reconcile_disposition_reason as BOTH required non-empty to discharge the violation. Optional -- absence is the undischarged state, not a defect; no schema-level requirement is imposed on any deployment_state (a required coupling would invalidate every existing handoff on write).

reconcile_disposition_reason.description: Free-text justification paired with reconcile_disposition -- read by coordinator_core/ops/handoff_reconcile.py's `_check_conservation` (D1 assertion) via the module-level `_DISPOSITION_REASON_FIELD` constant. Both fields must be non-empty for `_has_recorded_disposition` to clear a D1 conservation violation. Optional; no cross-field validation coupling to reconcile_disposition is enforced at the schema level -- see that field's description.

gate_evidence.description: Structured, machine-checkable evidence for a prose gate_dependency/blocked_by sentence -- the ratified declaration half of the C6 external-gate-evidence vocabulary (consumer already landed at claude-klabauter coordinator_core/reconcile/gate_eval.py, commit 7e69ecc1; this is what a caller assembles for it to read). Spec backlink: state/plan-sidecars/2026-07-27-gate-resolution-widen-and-migrate.c6-witness-set-ratification.md (the Director of Engineering, eng-director) -- that ratification is authoritative over the landed evaluator wherever the two disagree; the amendments below are rework on already-landed code, not a free authoring choice (Finding 1). A NEW witness source feeding evaluate_gate's existing clear/narrow/surface/not-cleared prose mechanism (rule 0, gated on covers_prose:true) -- never a fifth verdict class (Structural finding Part A). additionalProperties intentionally permissive, matching this file's convention elsewhere; the propertyNames guard below is the load-bearing restriction, not additionalProperties.

covers_prose.description: REQUIRED. Human assertion that legs[] fully cover what the prose gate_dependency/blocked_by sentence asserts. Checked FIRST by evaluate_gate's rule 0: only when this is explicitly true do the legs become authoritative and get AND-reduced onto the prose verdict; any other value (absent, or explicitly false) leaves prose dominant and every leg inert (D2a). This is not a partial-credit knob -- a record with covers_prose:false and a full legs[] array is valid and means 'these legs exist but do not yet fully discharge the prose sentence', a documented and expected shape for a partial backfill (three of C10's fifteen backfill targets are known to land here).

legs.description: REQUIRED, non-empty, FLAT array -- never nested. An empty legs[] is malformed and never vacuously frees the gate (the reducer treats it as indeterminate). Nesting was considered and rejected: it reintroduces a summary value that hides which half failed, the same last_gate_recheck vacuity this vocabulary exists to cure.

leg_id.description: REQUIRED. Stable per-leg identifier, unique within this record's legs[] -- enforced by cross-field/engine rule, not this JSON Schema (same division of labor as carried_items[].carry_id above: schema declares the field required, a cross-field gate enforces uniqueness). The landed evaluator defaults an absent leg_id to the literal string '<unknown>'; two defaulted legs would report identically and the flat list's entire reason for existing -- per-leg result attribution -- evaporates. Do not rely on that default.

kind.description: CLOSED ENUM discriminator selecting how repo/ref/expected/reason/note are shaped (record-level allOf below pins the per-kind shape) and which resolver predicate applies -- engine consumer: claude-klabauter coordinator_core/reconcile/gate_eval.py _evaluate_gate_evidence_leg. The first four names are carried VERBATIM from cutover.schema.json's confirmed_consumers[].verified_by.kind, but the SHAPE is not a verbatim carry-over: cutover resolves repo roots at the confirmed_consumers RECORD level from gate_source.repos[] and has no per-entry repo field, whereas gate_evidence has no record-level repo declaration at all, so repo: below is a genuine extension, not an inherited field (Finding 5). The next three are deliberately KEBAB-CASE (file-exists, frontmatter-field, commit-ancestor) even though the landed evaluator's own frozensets spell them snake_case (file_exists, frontmatter_field, commit_ancestor) -- kebab is the ratified authoring form (Finding 4: a mixed-casing discriminator is a live typo generator against a closed enum, and the ratification normalizes the newly-added five to kebab; deadline/human are single words and unaffected either way). Per-kind resolution: test-node-id -- a pytest node id the resolver re-runs; satisfied iff observed is True. probe-op-key -- an engine op-key the resolver re-invokes; satisfied iff observed is True. commit-sha -- a commit the resolver git-shows and pattern-matches; satisfied iff observed is True. sibling-commitment-ref -- an FK to a state/cross-repo-commitments/*.yaml record; satisfied iff observed is True. commit-ancestor -- distinct from commit-sha (ancestry, not content-match); the resolver runs git ancestry, satisfied iff observed is True; ref MUST name both ends (a bare SHA with an implicit default target is the same silent-wrong-tree failure the mandatory repo: rule exists to prevent). file-exists -- the resolver stats the path; satisfied iff observed == expected -- existence is never satisfaction (an artifact can exist and say nothing), so expected and note are both required on this kind alone, and where the checked artifact carries a machine-readable state field, frontmatter-field is mandatory instead and file-exists is inadmissible (an actioned cross-repo memo's real condition is status: actioned, not its presence in archive/). frontmatter-field -- the resolver reads the field; satisfied iff observed == expected -- the strongest of the four, converting 'the memo is actioned' into a machine fact. deadline -- no I/O: the resolver computes elapsed from the authored absolute ISO-8601 date carried in ref (never a relative expression); this is a PROMPT, not a satisfier, and is excluded from the AND-reduce toward freed. Three distinguishable signal classes exist and only this kind produces the middle one -- a leg that has been resolved, one that is merely aged with nothing left to re-derive (review-due), and one nobody has looked at yet -- never conflate these three. human -- declared-unresolvable by construction, always indeterminate; the honest alternative to prose that looks resolvable and never is. reason is REQUIRED non-empty here (the landed evaluator's own default of 'no reason authored' is explicitly not relied upon by this schema -- a reasonless human leg is a hiding place, not honest-indeterminate). An unrecognized kind value is schema-inadmissible by this closed enum; a pre-schema record reaching the evaluator with one is marked indeterminate exactly like a human leg, but the two are NOT the same fact -- one is a data defect this enum should have prevented, the other is deliberate declared indeterminacy -- and a triage report must be able to tell them apart (Finding 7).

repo.description: Registry key the leg resolves against (e.g. doe_claude, claude_klabauter) -- NEVER a filesystem path. REQUIRED on every kind except human and deadline (ruling 6 / Finding 6) -- do not infer a leg's repo from context; a resolver that infers resolves against the wrong tree silently. An unregistered repo value resolves read_ok:false at the resolver, which this module's predicate maps to indeterminate, never unsatisfied -- mirroring cutover's fail-closed unscanned-foreign-repo clause. Genuine EXTENSION of cutover's verified_by shape, not a verbatim carry (Finding 5) -- see the kind description above.

ref.description: The evidence reference, shaped per kind (record-level allOf below enforces the pairing): a pytest node id (test-node-id), an invokable op-key (probe-op-key), a full or abbreviated commit SHA (commit-sha), a state/cross-repo-commitments/*.yaml filename, bare or path-qualified (sibling-commitment-ref), '<commit-ish>@<target-ref>' naming both ends -- never a bare SHA (commit-ancestor), a repo-relative path (file-exists), '<repo-relative-path>#<field-name>' (frontmatter-field), or an absolute ISO-8601 date, never a relative expression (deadline). NOT CARRIED on kind=human -- reason carries the entire justification there instead.

expected.description: Equality-kind comparand. REQUIRED and typed per-kind (record-level allOf below): boolean on file-exists; non-null scalar on frontmatter-field. Not applicable to the five boolean-observed kinds (test-node-id, probe-op-key, commit-sha, sibling-commitment-ref, commit-ancestor), to deadline (whose predicate is the resolver's own elapsed computation), or to human (never machine-resolved) -- none of those compare an observation against an authored expectation. A null or absent expected on frontmatter-field collapses that kind into file-exists and re-opens the existence-is-not-satisfaction trap file-exists's own required note exists to flag -- do not author it that way.

reason.description: REQUIRED non-empty on kind=human only -- the entire justification for the declared-unresolvable kind. This schema requires it structurally precisely because the landed evaluator's own fallback ('no reason authored') is not an acceptable authored value -- a covers_prose:true block containing any human leg can never reach freed, and reason is the only accountability a human leg carries. Free prose, never machine-compared against anything.

note.description: Commentary, NEVER machine-read by the resolver or the reducer -- on a corpus that just spent this whole plan learning that prose gates do not resolve, do not put the real condition here; it belongs in ref/expected. REQUIRED non-empty on kind=file-exists only, where it must state what the existence check actually proves. Optional free text on every other kind.

ref.description: '<commit-ish>@<target-ref>' -- the '@' is load-bearing: a bare SHA with no '@' fails this pattern outright, which is deliberate (a bare SHA implies an implicit default target and re-opens the silent-wrong-tree failure the mandatory repo: rule exists to prevent, per Finding 6).
'<repo-relative-path>#<field-name>' -- exactly one '#', non-empty on both sides.

expected.description: Non-null scalar, REQUIRED. A null or absent expected collapses this kind into file-exists and re-opens the existence-is-not-satisfaction trap (ruling 2).

ref.description: Absolute ISO-8601 date (or date-time), NEVER a relative expression ('in 2 weeks', '+7d'). elapsed is resolver-computed from this value and is authoring-forbidden (see the propertyNames guard on this object).

last_gate_recheck.description: Timestamp of the last gate-recheck pass; stamped by the gate-recheck verb regardless of --cleared.

park_note.description: Optional single-line note recorded by the unconsume transition when a picked-up baton is returned to the shelf (why it was un-consumed). Written by handoff-transition.js unconsume --note / cs_unconsume_handoff.

shipped_in.description: The commit at which this baton was declared shipped (a caller-supplied ship commit), always a resolvable SHA, OR the sanctioned substantively-shipped-no-commit:<YYYY-MM-DD> stealth-skip token. Any set value is shape-validated by this pattern unconditionally; the date-gated *requirement* to set shipped_in on shipped handoffs lives in cross-field Rule A3a-2b (pre-cutoff shipped handoffs predating the convention are exempt from the requirement, not from value shape). Companion field shipped_in_kind tags which of the sanctioned resolutions produced this value — read that field's description before assuming this is a direct ship commit. The caller-supplied ship commit is DR-096 meaning 2; see DR-096 for the full taxonomy of how this value is resolved.

shipped_in_kind.description: Discriminant for how shipped_in was resolved — required whenever shipped_in is set (required-when-shipped, alongside shipped_in itself). Makes the *meaning* of shipped_in type-checkable by this tag instead of by regex-sniffing the string it points at. ship-commit = the commit at which this baton was declared shipped (the canonical case: a caller-supplied ship commit at write time). successor = the SHA belongs to a successor or the deliverable that resolved this baton (handoff_reconcile gate-a); the successor pointer itself lives in the existing succession fields (continued_into / disposed_successors), NOT duplicated here — this only tags that shipped_in's SHA was sourced from that lineage, not a direct ship commit. scope-derived = legacy/best-effort resolution from the baton's own scope paths (retired as the PREFERRED write-time strategy per DR-096, not eliminated as a write path outright: three in-process sha-less stampers — wsc_commit.py's pre-commit tail, /update-docs Phase 8, and boot_sweep's best-effort stamp — can each still select this kind when no caller-supplied sha is available; none is reached via a CLI --sha flag. Per the blast-radius audit (state/audits/2026-07-26-scope-derived-retirement-blast-radius.md), this kind appears ZERO times on disk across either repo's live or archived corpus — a short observation window since shipped_in_kind started being written, not a durable absence proof. Retiring this write path is orthogonal to the handoff archival backlog, not a drain measure for it. See DR-096 § Current state vs. target state for the corrected account before assuming this tag never appears on a freshly-written value). no-commit = shipped_in holds the substantively-shipped-no-commit:<date> token, not a SHA.

continued_into.description: Successor pointer for deployment_state=continued — handoff_id (hnd-<slug>-<6hex>) preferred, state/handoffs/... path fallback (pre-existing successors carry no handoff_id; no backfill). The tooth that keeps 'continued' from becoming liveness-guess abandonment: an automated writer that cannot name the successor cannot stamp continued. Required-when-continued (P4 narrow).

disposed_successors.description: Lineage-preservation edges written by distill.apply_disposal (C14) BEFORE a successor handoff is deleted: each entry is a successor's continued-into value (handoff_id preferred, path fallback — same shape as continued_into) for a successor that continued this record's work and was later disposed by /distill. Multi-valued (unlike continued_into, single-valued and deployment_state=continued-gated) because a parent can accumulate multiple disposed successors across separate /distill runs; each entry is append-only and never overwritten. Distinct from continued_into: this field is NOT deployment_state-conditional and is NOT itself the successor pointer for this record's own lifecycle — it is a reverse-pointing lineage record of OTHER records that pointed at this one and have since been deleted.

closed_reason.description: Deliberate-stop subtype for deployment_state=closed (human/session only, never automated — DR-084). cancelled = deliberate stop; displaced = replaced with NO lineage edge (with an edge it's continued, not closed); stale = overtaken by events. Deliberately NO crashed/orphaned value: a successor-less dead-holder has no automated terminal — it surfaces for adjudication. Required-when-closed (P4 narrow).

blocks.description: Stub IDs this stub blocks. Permitted on ANY kind as of C1 — the former roadmap-only cross-field gate was removed so the gate resolver can carry non-roadmap batons. (kind=roadmap-baton still REQUIRES this field, along with roadmap_id/stub_id/wave/blocked_by — enforced in the Python cross-field layer only (`_cf_spinoff_roadmap_requires_graph`), NOT in this file's allOf; relaxing the one did not weaken the other. roadmap_id remains genuinely roadmap-scoped and still rejects on other kinds.)

blocked_by.description: Stub IDs OR handoff_id values that block this stub (namespace decision already made — do not re-open: the mutating path already matches blocker_id in (stub_id, handoff_id), so the compute index accepting both here makes it agree with what mutation already does). Permitted on ANY kind as of C1 — the former roadmap-only cross-field gate was removed so the gate resolver can carry non-roadmap batons, and `ops/handoff_children.blocked_by_dependents` plus the d6 roadmap-baton-decline evidence text both read it on non-baton handoffs. (kind=roadmap-baton still REQUIRES this field, along with roadmap_id/stub_id/wave/blocks — enforced in the Python cross-field layer only (`_cf_spinoff_roadmap_requires_graph`, whose required list names blocked_by explicitly), NOT in this file's allOf, so a schema-only reader is not misled; relaxing the one did not weaken the other. roadmap_id remains genuinely roadmap-scoped and still rejects on other kinds — `_cf_graph_fields_roadmap_only`, whose gated set is roadmap_id ALONE.) Pattern is deliberately permissive (no whitespace, no path separator, no .md extension) rather than fit to the numeric stub_id families (<slug>-<N>) — live records include shapes like pacl-05-a, strang-10-C, strang-10-inject-anchor, cis-producer-locator that a narrower `^[a-z]+-\d{2}$`-style pattern would reject outright.

roadmap_id.description: Roadmap identifier. Roadmap-only (kind=roadmap-baton); cross-field rule rejects on other kinds.

stub_id.description: Globally-unique stub code (<slug>-<N>). Required by cross-field rule when kind=roadmap-baton.

wave.description: Serialization-order grouping within a sprint. Required by cross-field rule when kind=roadmap-baton.

cost.description: Estimation tier T0|T1|T2|T3. Cross-field rule enforces allowed values when present.

suggested_priority.description: Advisory execution-priority signal an EM may attach to this handoff at authoring time. Optional (not nullable — absence already covers 'no suggestion'; a redundant null representation was reviewed out, see Finding 4 / review-integrator). Enum is the priority-ledger domain (priority-ledger.schema.json's urgent|high|medium|low|none) MINUS 'none' — an EM has no reason to author an explicit clear; absence of the field already covers that case. Advisory only: the PM-owned priority ledger (state/priority-ledger/) is the authoritative tier and lives on a deliberately separate surface — this field never overrides it, and that separation (not memory) is what keeps 'advisory never overrides authoritative' structural. Do NOT add a pm_priority field to this frontmatter to compensate; the tier split is the point. NEGATIVE-SPEC: no inherited_from / priority_predecessor field is permitted on this frontmatter either — priority does not chain hop-to-hop the way carry_id does. No backfill of pre-existing handoffs, consistent with this schema's origin_* no-backfill policy.

category.description: Workstream category. Required by cross-field rule for handoffs created >= 2026-05-29. 'uncategorized' is the null-object sentinel for the one-time backfill normalizer only. 'queue-derived-baton' marks a handoff authored as a queue-triage terminus (solo or themed baton) rather than an ordinary session handoff — class-filterable per docs/plans/2026-07-23-queue-triage-terminates-in-batons.md; interim scaffolding uses 'infra' and hand-edits to this value until claude-klabauter's coordinator-doc-new default is updated (C9 memo). WIRE PROJECTION: this field is emitted into the cockpit contract as 'workstream_type' — same axis, two names, a 1:1 passthrough at claude-klabauter coordinator_core/ops/emit/sections/handoffs.py:401. Adding a value here is NOT sufficient on its own: the cockpit WorkstreamType Literal (coordinator_core/contract/cockpit_schema/entities/deliverable_spine.py) is a closed set and must gain the same value. A handoff carrying a value that Literal does not know is quarantined per-record into the emission's 'malformed' bucket with a logged reason (caught at emit/sections/handoffs.py:436-449) — the emission RUN still completes, but that baton vanishes from the wire and no fleet consumer can see or filter it. See docs/wiki/queue-terminus-doctrine.md § The cockpit projection.

summary.description: One-line session summary (<=140 chars). Required by cross-field rule for handoffs created >= 2026-05-29. Length enforced by cross-field rule.

reviewed_at_workstream_complete.description: Review marker written by /workstream-complete and /handoff. Format: '<sha-range> <reviewer> <YYYY-MM-DD>'. Absent on spinoff-kind handoffs.

completeness_checklist.description: Install/onboarding completeness items. Each item: '<class>: <assertion text> [probe: <shell-command>]'. Opt-in — intended for install/onboarding batons only.

supersedes.description: Conditional-live orientation-supersession field. Permitted only on kind=spinoff (cross-field rule enforced). Distinct from the terminal memo supersedes:/superseded_by: coupling.

additional_predecessors.description: Fan-in merge edges — additional parent handoff paths beyond the primary predecessor. Optional. Each entry is a path string to a predecessor handoff. Cross-field rules enforce: no duplicate entries within the array; no entry duplicating the primary predecessor field. Population is engine-derived, not PM-directed: baton_assemble resolves the fan-in legs via _resolve_held_handoff_for_session and writes this field at successor-scaffold time (d1) from the same resolved list it uses to stamp each leg's own continued_into up-edge (d6*). An EM may still supply legs by hand via coordinator-doc-new --additional-predecessor.

forked_from.description: Spinoff branch-point ancestry (lineage/render-only). Permitted only on kind=spinoff by cross-field kind-gate. NOT followed by the LoE aggregation primitive (DR-014 effort-isolation preserved); present for DAG rendering and lineage tracing only. Requires PM direction.

deliverable_id.description: Durable deliverable join key. Minted once at the earliest artifact (roadmap-spinoff stub or first plan/handoff) and carried verbatim by every downstream artifact. dlv-<stub_id> for roadmap-stub origins; dlv-<slug>-<6hex> for plan/handoff origins. Cross-field rule enforces 'dlv-' prefix when non-null. Null for pre-backfill artifacts. Spec backlink: claude-klabauter:pln-fleet-deliverable-spine-identity-and-facets-2b331c § D1

deliverable_ids.description: Plural fan-in sibling of deliverable_id (nested-field-additive, 8.1.0 -> 8.2.0) — the join-key set a successor unifying multiple predecessor batons inherits when it carries more than one deliverable forward. Same 'dlv-' pattern as deliverable_id on every array entry; deliverable_id itself is RETAINED, unchanged in meaning, and remains the single-deliverable case's field — this is an added carrier, not a replacement. Null or an absent key both mean 'no plural set authored'; an empty array is not the same as null (reserved for a future 'explicitly zero' distinction, unused as of this bump). No cross-field allOf coupling to deliverable_id is imposed — a record may carry either, both, or neither. Cross-repo ask: cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-19-claude-klabauter-em-baton-schema-bump-role-axis-and-pickup-doctrine.md § Ask 1.

initiative.description: FK to the initiative entity (state/initiatives/<id>.yaml). Nullable — not all work belongs to a named initiative. Cross-field rule enforces non-empty string when non-null. Spec backlink: claude-klabauter:pln-fleet-deliverable-spine-identity-and-facets-2b331c § D2

caption.description: One-sentence business-legible outcome line. NOT an engineering title or filename — authored for CEO-board legibility (e.g. 'Shipped the Example-Fleet Pro billing flow'). Optional; authored at creation time.

status_reason.description: Free-text one-liner explaining the current status (e.g. 'abandoned — superseded by X'). Optional authored field; carried into the cockpit emission as a product-legibility facet.

owner.description: Authoring workstream or EM identifier. Nullable; carried forward from the earliest artifact for the deliverable.

origin_session.description: Originating-session provenance — the session UUID in which this fork was spawned. DISTINCT from predecessor (continuation spine, always none for forks), forked_from (branch-point ancestry, handoff-path), and deliverable_id (dlv- grouping key). Scalar 0..1. Id format: global UUID, no prefix (already globally unique). Backfill=null for pre-existing forks; no migration. Spec backlink: pln-structured-originating-session-8b505c § Field shape

origin_handoff.description: Originating-handoff provenance — the active baton path (state/handoffs/…) at fork-authoring time. DISTINCT from predecessor (continuation spine), forked_from (branch-point ancestry, also a handoff-path but lineage/render-only), and deliverable_id (dlv- grouping key). Scalar 0..1. Id format: state/handoffs/… path (inherently namespaced). This is the sole origin_* field that is a handoff-DAG edge (registered in walk-handoff-dag.js EDGE_KIND_META); the other three are cross-entity refs. Backfill=null for pre-existing forks; no migration. Spec backlink: pln-structured-originating-session-8b505c § Field shape

origin_handoff_id.description: ID-companion for origin_handoff (C2, add-not-swap) — the originating baton's handoff_id, resolved and stamped at author time from the SAME baton origin_handoff names (never a different one). Path-independent, survives the originating baton's archival/rename; origin_handoff remains the human-legible display path. Null when the originating baton has no handoff_id (pre-existing artifact, no backfill) or origin_handoff is null. Never-silently-disagree cross-field rule (origin_handoff/origin_handoff_id must resolve to the same artifact when both non-null) is owned by C3, not this schema file. Spec backlink: pln-lifecycle-vocab-c2-durable-cro-991bd4 § C2

origin_plan_id.description: Originating-plan provenance — the plan under execution when this fork was spawned. DISTINCT from predecessor (continuation spine), forked_from (branch-point ancestry), and deliverable_id (dlv- grouping key). Scalar 0..1. Id format: pln-prefixed (e.g. pln-structured-originating-session-8b505c). Cross-entity ref — NOT a handoff-DAG edge; rag's origin_edges projection owns the durable query surface. Backfill=null for pre-existing forks; no migration. Spec backlink: pln-structured-originating-session-8b505c § Field shape

plan_ids.description: Plural fan-in sibling of origin_plan_id (nested-field-additive, 8.1.0 -> 8.2.0) — the plan-provenance set a successor unifying multiple predecessor batons inherits when more than one plan was under execution across the merged lineage. Same string shape as origin_plan_id on every array entry (pln-prefixed by convention, unenforced by pattern here exactly as origin_plan_id itself is unenforced); origin_plan_id is RETAINED, unchanged in meaning, and remains the single-plan case's field — this is an added carrier, not a replacement. Null or an absent key both mean 'no plural set authored'. No cross-field allOf coupling to origin_plan_id is imposed — a record may carry either, both, or neither. Cross-entity ref, same as origin_plan_id — NOT a handoff-DAG edge. Cross-repo ask: cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-19-claude-klabauter-em-baton-schema-bump-role-axis-and-pickup-doctrine.md § Ask 1.

origin_goal_id.description: Originating-goal provenance — the goal(s) tagged at fork-authoring time. Array (string[] | null) because multi-goal forks are real (a roadmap serving multiple goals; many-to-many InitiativeSummary.goals[]). DISTINCT from predecessor (continuation spine), forked_from (branch-point ancestry), and deliverable_id (dlv- grouping key). Each entry is goal-prefixed kebab-case (e.g. goal-shipping-velocity) — matches the goal.schema.json id field scheme. Cross-entity ref — NOT a handoff-DAG edge; rag's origin_edges projection fans array entries into N edge rows. Backfill=null for pre-existing forks; no migration. Spec backlink: pln-structured-originating-session-8b505c § Field shape

handoff_id.description: Durable stable ID for this handoff/spinoff record, path-independent (survives archival move/rename). Minted via coordinator-doc-new's _mint_artifact_id(prefix="hnd", slug) at scaffold time — hnd-<slug>-<6hex>. OPTIONAL on new records going forward, but POLICY REVERSED (DR-102, C10) for the live corpus: state/handoffs/*.md records that predated this field were BACKFILLED via coordinator/lib/backfill-handoff-id.py (idempotent; frontmatter-primitives seam; script removed post-backfill, its job done) — this supersedes the prior no-backfill prose, which was consistent with this schema's origin_* no-migration policy but does not hold for handoff_id itself. archive/handoffs/ remains grandfathered (out of scope for the reversal), matching DR-096 §5's precedent for shipped_in on archived batons. This is the join key C2's predecessor_id/origin_handoff_id ID-companion ancestry fields resolve against — backfilling it serves LINEAGE tracking only and does NOT de-collide the gate index (which joins on id/stub_id, a separate namespace). Spec backlink: pln-lifecycle-vocab-c2-durable-cro-991bd4 § C1; DR-102

recovers_session.description: recovery-kind only: session-id of the crashed session being reconstructed. OPTIONAL, no cross-field enforcement (yet) — a future cross-field rule could require this to be non-null when kind=recovery, but that gate is left as a follow-up (see bin/lib/schema.js CROSS_FIELD_RULES['handoff'] comment).

handoff_phase.description: The plan→execute seam axis on kind: session-handoff AND canonical kind: roadmap-baton — it is NOT session-handoff-only. Absence ≡ continuation (going-forward default). OPTIONAL. The kind-gate MUST resolve the roadmap side through kind_values_for_canonical('roadmap-baton'), never a bare kind == 'roadmap-baton' literal: that canonical resolves to {roadmap-baton, spinoff-roadmap}, and real roadmap batons on disk carry kind: spinoff-roadmap — a literal gate would never fire on them. Admitting this field on roadmap-baton is NOT backfilling it — widening this validation gate does not widen any stamping predicate. Cross-field rules (stamp-required-when-execution: _cf_execution_stamp_required; kind-gate: _cf_handoff_phase_kind_gate) live in claude-klabauter/coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py's _HANDOFF_CROSS_FIELD_RULES list. Spec backlink: pln-first-class-execution-handoff--40a6e5 § C1

baton_role.description: The inheritability axis (nested-field-additive, 8.1.0 -> 8.2.0): work = a unit of work a session or run may inherit (e.g. an ordinary continuation handoff, a spinoff carrying real work, a roadmap stub). record = a session's own scratch identity, or any artifact filed rather than picked up (a spike verdict, a session-start baton.json) — never offered as inheritable work. OPTIONAL. Absence ≡ unknown, and unknown is NOT inheritable — a consumer checks by POSITIVE MATCH (`baton_role == "work"`), never via a defaulted `.get(..., "work")` and never via a normalizer backfill: `handoff.normalize` MUST NEVER stamp this field onto an existing unstamped record, since sweeping 'work' across the legacy corpus would convert an honestly-unknown population into a false assertion in one commit. That not-inheritable-when-absent rule is scoped to NEW consumers reading this axis (the unification held-set, /mise-en-place's inheritance set) — it does NOT gate /pickup admitting an artifact the operator explicitly named; an operator naming a path is the authority, and this field is not a second gate on their instruction. Distinct from two axes it sits beside on this same schema, and must not be folded with either: `kind` (session-handoff | spinoff | roadmap-baton | goal-seed | roadmap-seed | recovery) answers where this record came from, not what may inherit it — a spinoff can carry baton_role: work despite kind alone never implying that. `handoff_phase` (continuation | execution) is the plan→execute seam on an already-inheritable record and is a different axis entirely — do NOT use the string 'execution' as a baton_role value; a record can validly carry `handoff_phase: execution` alongside `baton_role: work` on the same frontmatter block, and the two must never be conflated. Ratifying review: state/subagent-share/bc70d292-1669-4531-aaa9-845c1b8bb79c/coordinatoreng-director-d8ff2cfd.md. Cross-repo ask: cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-19-claude-klabauter-em-baton-schema-bump-role-axis-and-pickup-doctrine.md § Ask 2.

execution_authorized_by.description: The PM/session that authorized execution. OPTIONAL — one of the four-field execution-authorization stamp (by/at/sha/note); required-together enforcement (_cf_execution_stamp_required) lives in claude-klabauter/coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py's _HANDOFF_CROSS_FIELD_RULES list when handoff_phase=execution. Spec backlink: pln-first-class-execution-handoff--40a6e5 § C1

execution_authorized_at.description: ISO 8601 date-time of authorization. OPTIONAL — one of the four-field execution-authorization stamp (by/at/sha/note); required-together enforcement (_cf_execution_stamp_required) lives in claude-klabauter/coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py's _HANDOFF_CROSS_FIELD_RULES list when handoff_phase=execution. Spec backlink: pln-first-class-execution-handoff--40a6e5 § C1

execution_authorized_sha.description: git-hash-object of the plan body at authorization (the content-binding witness /pickup recomputes; schema shape-only). OPTIONAL — one of the four-field execution-authorization stamp (by/at/sha/note); required-together enforcement (_cf_execution_stamp_required) lives in claude-klabauter/coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py's _HANDOFF_CROSS_FIELD_RULES list when handoff_phase=execution. Spec backlink: pln-first-class-execution-handoff--40a6e5 § C1

execution_authorized_note.description: The verbatim PM utterance that named execution. The FOURTH field of the stamp: plan-execute-session-split.md § Pinned conventions pins the stamp as a byte-identical FOUR-field contract (by/at/sha/note); note is the self-attesting field — a stamp without a note that names execution signals the write-bar may not have been met. Do NOT drop it. OPTIONAL — required-together enforcement (_cf_execution_stamp_required) lives in claude-klabauter/coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py's _HANDOFF_CROSS_FIELD_RULES list when handoff_phase=execution. Spec backlink: pln-first-class-execution-handoff--40a6e5 § C1

carry_id.description: Stable identity for one carried item, minted ONCE (cf-<slug>-<6hex>) the first time the item is carried, then threaded byte-identical through every successor handoff regardless of how the item's prose is re-worded hop to hop. This is the anti-evasion tooth: the gate (coordinator_core.ops.handoff_carry_gate, claude-klabauter) keys on carry_id, never on description text, so re-wording an item never loses the thread. A new item (first appearance) mints a fresh carry_id; an item continuing from the predecessor keeps its predecessor's carry_id byte-identical.

description.description: Human-readable one-liner for the item — free to reword hop to hop; carry_id (not this text) is the identity key.

disposition.description: carried = still open, no sanctioned exit yet — legal at any carry depth: an item may be carried indefinitely so long as each hop declares its state. closed = terminated in place (disposition_detail names why, mirrors deployment_state: closed's closed_reason vocabulary). spun_off = forked into its own baton (disposition_detail names the spinoff handoff path/id). blocked = the sanctioned exit for a genuine external dependency (e.g. hardware-gated Windows-host validation) — remains visible and explicit rather than silently re-carried; disposition_detail must name the concrete blocking condition, not restate 'blocked'.

disposition_detail.description: Required whenever disposition != carried (cross-field rule _cf_carried_items_shape in coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py, claude-klabauter) — names the closure reason, the spinoff target, or the concrete external blocker. A disposition of closed/spun_off/blocked with no disposition_detail is the exact 'operator remembers' shape this field exists to eliminate, so the rule rejects it.

first_seen_handoff_id.description: handoff_id of the handoff where this carry_id was first minted. Null when unknown (pre-existing item backfilled without history). Provenance only — not consulted by the gate.

carried_items.description: Machine-readable replacement for the free-prose '_(carried via N handoffs)_' annotation under `## Carried Forward` — see coordinator/skills/handoff/SKILL.md § Cascading unresolved items. Each entry is gate-checked by coordinator_core.ops.handoff_carry_gate (claude-klabauter) before the handoff is written: the gate refuses a missing/non-string carry_id, an unrecognized disposition, and a terminal disposition (closed/spun_off/blocked) with an empty disposition_detail. It does NOT gate on carry depth — carries are indefinite so long as each hop declares the item's state.
